heroHeadline: Spain Cuts Ceuta Minors Count to ~1,500 as Sánchez Convenes Security Council Nearly a Month Into Crisis
heroSubtitle: Spain's Interior Ministry revises its estimate of unaccompanied migrant minors in Ceuta down from 2,168 to roughly 1,500 after finding duplicate case entries in its database, while PM Pedro Sánchez convenes an extraordinary National Security Council meeting as officials acknowledge the city remains 'very far' from normality nearly four weeks after the July 30 mass crossing; Madrid separately unveils plans to reform Spain's asylum law to align with the EU's Migration and Asylum Pact, and Spain's anti-racism observatory logs nearly 9,600 hate posts tied to the crisis in just two days.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
